question.problem: Using the extended Euclidean algorithm, compute integers $u$ and $v$ such that $80u+35v=\text{gcd}(80,35).$ What is the value of $u+v?$
question.worked_solution:
We will use the extended Euclidean algorithm. First, we apply the forward reduction:

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}80 & = & 35\cdot 2 & + & 10 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 35 & = & 10\cdot 3 & + & 5 \\  & ↙ &  & ↙ &  \\ 10 & = & 5\cdot 2 & + & 0\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, $\text{gcd}(80,35)=5.$

Solving for the remainders (the rightmost terms) in the equations above, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}10 & =80-35\cdot 2 \\ 5 & =35-10\cdot 3.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we back-substitute:

$$
\begin{aligned}5 & =35-10\cdot 3 \\  & =35-[80-35\cdot 2]\cdot 3 \\  & =35\cdot 7-80\cdot 3 \\  & =80\cdot (-3)+35\cdot 7\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $u=-3$ and $v=7.$

Finally, 

$$
u+v=(-3)+7=4.
$$
